page: Microsoft Azure D16plds_v6 is an ARM-based virtual machine belonging to the Dpldsv6 server family. It is powered by a Microsoft Neoverse-N2 processor with 16 dedicated physical cores and 16 vCPUs running at 3.4 GHz. The architecture features a 128 MB L3 cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 64 KB L1d cache per core, operating under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. This instance is configured with 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per core, and includes 945 GB of local storage with Premium Storage capabilities.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong memory subsystem capabilities, with large-block read bandwidth reaching 307.54 GB/sec and write bandwidth at 124.58 GB/sec, both placing in the top 25% tier. Single-threaded gzip compression is also strong at 33.08 GB/sec. Standard computational benchmarks, such as stress-ng and Geekbench, show average tier performance, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 14736.0 and a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 33160.55. Large language model inference on a medium 7B model delivers an average text generation speed of 14.24 tokens per second, though prompt processing is relatively weak at 24.62 tokens per second.

The D16plds_v6 offers qualitative cost efficiency for workloads requiring dedicated ARM compute resources without the overhead of high memory allocations. The 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio makes it suitable for compute-bound tasks that do not demand massive memory footprints. Tradeoffs include the lack of AVX or AMX instruction sets and the absence of a dedicated GPU. This server is well-suited for applications such as web serving, software compilation, multi-threaded decompression tasks, and lightweight database operations.
